item.title: Tamatsukuri Onsen: The Beauty Hot Spring of the Gods — Guide
item.description: Tamatsukuri Onsen, near Matsue, is one of the oldest documented hot springs in Japan, praised as far back as the eighth-century Izumo Fudoki for waters that make the skin beautiful — a ‘beauty bath’ reputation it trades on to this day. Ryokan line a small river fringed with willows and cherry trees running through the resort, and the town leans into its mythology: the name means ‘jewel-making’, because this was historically a centre for carving magatama, the comma-shaped gem beads sacred in ancient Japan, and shops still sell them as good-luck charms.
